question.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $\frac{5-9a}{2}$ whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to $7.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-9a}{2} & \le -7 & \text{or} &  & \frac{5-9a}{2} & \ge 7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods. (Remember that whenever we multiply or divide by a negative number, we have to flip the inequality signs.)

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5-9a}{2} & \le -7 &  &  & \frac{5-9a}{2} & \ge 7 \\ 5-9a & \le -14 &  &  & 5-9a & \ge 14 \\ -9a & \le -19 &  &  & -9a & \ge 9 \\ 9a & \ge 19 &  &  & 9a & \le -9 \\ a & \ge \frac{19}{9} &  &  & a & \le -1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}a & \le -1 & \text{or} &  & a & \ge \frac{19}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
